repo_prior_art.cite: exp_saturation_exacthit_deficiency_design: exact-hit information deficiency and minimax design for ranking exact treatment saturations; it does not give a sharp compatible coupling image.

published_prior_art.cite: HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 optimizes conservative design-based variance bounds under interference and complex designs; GaoGeQian2025 gives exact multi-marginal identified sets, but neither states this exact-slice covariance image.
GaoGeQian2025 formulates exact causal multi-marginal identified sets and quadratic objectives via MOT; the displayed LP is the finite specialization after Theorem 1.
BairdEtAl2018 optimizes power under maintained structure; HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 optimizes variance estimators, not allocations over the proposed exact coupling set.
LiDing2017 supplies finite-population CLTs and Joo2025 studies fixed-covariance Gaussian minimax regret, but neither optimizes a sharp covariance ambiguity set.
AronowGreenLee2014 supplies the bivariate Fréchet--Hoeffding sharp-variance reduction.
Joo2025 treats a fixed covariance Gaussian game and GuggenbergerHuang2025 numerically approximates minimax-regret rules; neither couples the design, coupling, and selector optimizations.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The closest omitted comparator is Harshaw, Middleton, and Sävje (2026), which studies optimized conservative variance estimation under interference and complex experimental designs; distinguish its quadratic-bound program explicitly from the proposed sharp coupling image.

novelty_flags.label: GaoGeQian2025 bibliography and related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The proposal calls Gao--Ge--Qian an ICLR paper, but the published paper is in AISTATS 2025 (PMLR 258), so the bibliographic comparison must be corrected.

novelty_flags.label: GuggenbergerHuang2025 bibliography and related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: arXiv:2503.10932 is titled 'On the numerical approximation of minimax regret rules via fictitious play,' not 'Minimax Treatment Choice with Finite-Sample Guarantees.'

soundness_flags.label: ass:common-welfare-tie
soundness_flags.one_line: The equality of all exact-slice means is a proposal-specific local-boundary restriction, not a standard condition under the cited name; Joo2025 does not formulate this finite-population margin restriction.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2 (thm:sharp-support-lp)
soundness_flags.one_line: Once Lambda and Sigma are defined, optimizing a linear trace functional over the finite lambda polytope is directly an LP, so this cannot stand as an independent substantive theorem.

soundness_flags.label: Uhat and Theorem 4
soundness_flags.one_line: The observed cell mean is undefined on the positive-probability event that a target assignment cell receives no cluster, yet Uhat and its finite-C regret expectation are used without a fallback or an alternative always-defined estimator.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorems 1--4 / technical_internal_limitation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The assignment-cell marginal table f is fixed external planning information; a one-shot trial does not prospectively identify it exactly.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The covariance image and robust-design conclusions are conditional on f and the common-tie restriction.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published record identifies the venue as the 28th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, not ICLR.
The manuscript is titled 'On the numerical approximation of minimax regret rules via fictitious play' and studies discretized nature actions and fictitious play.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 4.1--4.2, 'Local Uniform CLT of the Reward Estimator' and plug-in MVN rule
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Joo assumes a local uniform CLT for a reward estimator and studies fixed-covariance Gaussian minimax regret; it does not formulate the proposed equality of all finite-population exact-slice means or convergence of assignment-cell margins.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Harshaw--Middleton--Sävje (2026) and state a theorem-level separation: their admissible quadratic upper bounds versus this full compatible covariance-set image and allocation problem.
Make Uhat total by specifying an empty-cell fallback with a proof that it is asymptotically negligible, or replace it by an always-defined Horvitz--Thompson-style estimator.

Move the LP observation into the proof of the covariance-image theorem, and promote a genuinely nontrivial result such as an explicit facet, strict comparison to a named conservative bound, or a computable design corollary.
Retag the common-welfare equality as a justified local-regime assumption and state why exact policy ties are operationally relevant for the intended saturation application.

recommended_next_step: Revise this angle: correct and expand the literature comparison, repair the estimator definition, and consolidate the definitional LP claim before advancing the sharp covariance-set kernel to Stage 0.
